what_its_for: This medicine is used to temporarily relieve minor aches and pains in your muscles and joints. It can help with pain from arthritis, backaches, sprains, strains, and bruises. Lidocaine numbs the area to reduce pain, while menthol creates a cool, soothing feeling on your skin.
how_to_take: Use this medicine only on your skin — never swallow it. Clean and dry the area of skin where you have pain before applying. If using a patch, peel off the backing and press the patch firmly onto your skin. If using a cream or gel, rub a small amount into the painful area. Wash your hands well after applying, unless you are treating your hands. Do not cover the treated area with tight bandages unless your doctor tells you to.
dosing: For most adults and children 12 years and older: Apply to the painful area up to 3 to 4 times a day, or as directed on the product label. Do not use more than the recommended amount. For patches, do not wear more than one patch at a time and do not cut the patch unless the label says it is okay. Follow the exact directions on your product package, as different brands may have slightly different instructions.
missed_dose: This medicine is used as needed for pain, so there is no set dosing schedule to follow. If you forget to apply it when you have pain, simply apply it when you remember. Do not use extra amounts to make up for a missed application.
storage: Store at room temperature, away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Keep away from children and pets. Used patches still contain medicine — fold them in half with the sticky sides together and throw them in the trash out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush patches down the toilet.
what_to_avoid: Do not use this medicine on broken, irritated, sunburned, or damaged skin. Do not use it near your eyes, mouth, or on your genitals. Do not apply heat (like a heating pad or hot water bottle) to the treated area, as this can increase the risk of side effects. Avoid using it on large areas of your body. Do not use it with other numbing or lidocaine-containing products at the same time unless your doctor approves.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor or seek medical help right away if you notice: a severe allergic reaction (rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, difficulty breathing), irregular heartbeat, dizziness, confusion, or feeling faint. Also call your doctor if your pain gets worse or does not improve after 7 days of use, if the area becomes very red, swollen, or blistered, or if you accidentally swallow any of this product.
when_it_works: Most people feel relief within 30 minutes to 1 hour of applying the medicine. The cooling or numbing effect may start sooner. This medicine provides temporary relief only — it does not treat the cause of your pain. If your pain continues for more than 7 days, talk to your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnant or breastfeeding women should ask their doctor before using this product. Children under 12 years old should not use this medicine unless directed by a doctor. Elderly patients should use with caution and avoid applying to large areas of skin. People with liver disease or heart conditions should talk to their doctor before using, since lidocaine can be absorbed through the skin and may affect these conditions.
